findings_addressed.oracle: capstone.Cs(CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_64).disasm(payload, 0, count=4) applied to the same NOP payload; each field (address, mnemonic, operands, size, bytes) is checked field-by-field against capstone output — capstone is independent of the bridge's _get_disassembler code path
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/bridges/hex_editor.py line 6750, change '"mnemonic": insn.mnemonic' to '"mnemonic": insn.mnemonic + "_bad"' — the assertion 'actual_insn["mnemonic"] == mnemonic' would then fail because the bridge emits "nop_bad" while capstone returns "nop"

notes: G0137 was a weak N8 (existence/type-only check for a behaviour test). The test was hardened in-place: after asserting the key subset is present, each instruction field is now validated against an independent capstone decode of the same NOP payload. The sibling test test_disassemble_matches_independent_capstone_decode uses INT3 bytes; this test uses NOP bytes, so both cover different payloads and are complementary rather than redundant. Deletion was not appropriate.
